items.note: The hovered product card turns one step darker and its title gets an underline, as the spec says. It sits among borderless cream cards with coloured pictogram covers, below cream filter pills with ink selection and dots, under a yolk header band with a sagging arc. The state reads clearly and in the system's language. The band itself looks empty: in this capture its product vignette is missing and only scattered confetti shows, where the reference hero (02) holds a full scene.

At night the hovered card lifts from indigo to a lighter violet-indigo with an underlined title. The pills turn indigo with a white selected pill, which is a faithful navy night palette in the manner of 03. The yellow band again shows only confetti because its vignette was not in view, and the footer ends in a white bottom bar.

On the phone the first card's cream turns darker on hover. The compact yellow band has a short sag and a small bag-and-cloud cluster tucked in the corner, as in the reference phone (04). Chunky pills sit on their ledges and the filter row scrolls. Clear and on-language; the only weakness is that the sort select and checkbox stack loosely and push the cards down.

The product has a large cover, so its header band turns cream, as the spec asks. The band carries a good price-tag scene: a crescent-shaded tag, a hexagon on a round-cap string, a blue disc and sparkles. Below the blue add-to-cart pill, an ink pill confirmation with a sparkle and a 'view cart' link appears, and the cart badge updates. The next step is obvious, and the craft is close to the reference's composed panels.

At night the header band is indigo with the same tag scene. The selected colour tile has a white border and the confirmation becomes a white pill with ink text. This reads clearly and is close to the night palette of 03. It is let down by the white bottom bar under the indigo footer, the one light strip on the page.

On the phone the cover follows the title straight away and the tag cluster sits in the band's corner. The full-width blue pill is followed by a wide ink confirmation card with a yellow sparkle and an underlined 'view cart'. The confirmation is legible and in the system's language. It is a block rather than a pill toast, which is slightly heavier than the reference's compact pieces.

The cart opens on a blue band with a real scene: a yellow crescent-shaded basket holding a pink and an orange item, a white star, a sparkle and a cloud, about 40% of the band, in the spirit of 02. The checkout sits in a cream panel like the form in 09. Each empty field has a 2px danger border, a solid alert glyph and a short instruction, and the blue place-order pill is below. The errors and the fix are clear.

The same blue band and basket scene sits over indigo panels. The error borders and messages lighten to a coral that stays legible on indigo, and the steppers and remove buttons become indigo circles and pills. This is a coherent night version, and the state reads as clearly as in light.

The compact blue band has the basket cluster in its corner. The cart and checkout stack as cream panels; the errored fields have danger borders and alert lines, followed by a full-width blue pill. This is clear and on-language. The first screen shows only the cart summary, so the errors sit below the fold with no summary at the top.

Keyboard focus is on the 'Cart' top-bar link, shown as a flush, square-cornered blue box around the text that looks like a browser default. The reference's focus (11) is a rounded ring offset 2px from a pill. The rest of the screen is the faithful catalog, but the state itself is cruder than the reference.

At night the same text link gets a square yellow box. It is visible, but sharp-cornered and tight against the label, unlike the rounded, offset ring the system uses on pills. A faint ghost of the band's vignette card shows inside the yellow band.

On the phone, focus lands on the ink cart pill and shows as a blue rounded ring offset 2px around the pill's ledge. That is exactly the reference's focus-visible treatment (11), and it is unmistakable which control is active.

The shop band is a real product vignette on yellow: three overlapping white cards (an item card, a filter row with an ink pill, an added-to-cart note) with a star, a sparkle, a crescent disc and a two-colour disc. That is the reference's vignette idea (01) done well. The product covers are flat, crescent-shaded pictograms, each its own subject: a tote, a backpack, a sweater, a tee, a coat on a hanger, a mug, an egg in a skillet and towels. On the grid they fill well under the 60–70% the spec asks for, and the duffel, a pink pill with a blue disc, reads as a toggle switch.

The detail band carries a big price-tag scene: a crescent-shaded yellow tag, a round-cap string to a hexagon, a blue disc behind and pink and orange sparkles. It is wide, layered and about its subject, in the spirit of 02's hero art. The large cover's tote fills it well with a clean shade edge, and the colour swatches are simple shaded discs.

The sweater cover is a clear, flat, blue crew-neck with darker crescent edges and a yellow collar on orange, with one sparkle. It reads at once and is crafted at the reference's spot-pictogram level (07). The band reuses the shared price-tag scene, and the small orange discs are size swatches.

The cart band shows a basket holding two crescent-shaded items with a star, a sparkle and a cloud on blue, a composed scene rather than a sticker. The empty-cart composition, a tilted basket with a round-cap handle, a cloud and a sparkle on cream, pictures its subject and is its own drawing. Both are close to the reference's flat kit.

The vignette cards build with the right fade and short rise, but the frames show them fading out and back in again and again rather than building once. That is busier than the reference's calm one-time build, and it is why page captures can catch the band empty. The product page's motion is just a static disc row.

findings.summary: The shop band's vignette cards loop their build instead of playing it once, so captures often catch the band with its cards invisible. The desktop catalog's first screen then shows a large empty yellow band with scattered confetti. The spec says the build runs once and the content is complete without the runtime class.
Keyboard focus on top-bar text links is still a flush, square-cornered box (blue by day, yellow at night), while pills get the reference's rounded ring offset 2px (11). Open since rc.2.

In dark mode the footer ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer, the one light strip on a night page. The spec still puts the bar on `surface.inverse`, which is white in the dark table. Named in rc.3 and still open.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons … (dark) `color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`

findings.summary: On the catalog grid the cover pictograms fill only about 40–45% of their covers, so the covers read as mostly empty colour. One pictogram, a pink pill with a blue disc for a bag, reads as a toggle switch rather than its subject. The reference's spot pictograms (07) fill their plates, and each one can be named at a glance.
